title: SAT Math 4 — Linear Inequalities Quiz
question: Five SAT-style questions on linear inequalities, with full working.
intro: Five questions on linear inequalities. **Show your working before you choose or type an answer.**

questions.title: Flip the sign
questions.solution_title: Collect x on the side where it stays positive
questions.solution:
\[\begin{aligned} -3x + 12 &\ge 2x + 2 \\ 10 &\ge 5x \\ 2 &\ge x \end{aligned}\]

\[\boxed{x \le 2}\]

If you divide by \(-5\) instead, remember to flip: \(x \le 2\) again, not \(x \ge 2\).

questions.title: Least score needed
questions.prompt:
A student scored 78, 85 and 90 on three tests.

What is the least score on the fourth test that makes the mean of the four tests at least 85?
questions.solution_title: Mean at least 85 means total at least 340

questions.title: Write the inequality
questions.prompt:
A bakery sells pastizzi for €0.60 each and qassatat for €0.90 each.

It must earn at least €270 in a day. It sells \(p\) pastizzi and \(q\) qassatat.

Which inequality models this?
questions.solution:
Money from pastizzi: \(0.6p\). Money from qassatat: \(0.9q\).

“At least €270” is \(\ge\):

\[\boxed{0.6p + 0.9q \ge 270}\]

questions.title: Count the integers
questions.prompt:
\[-7 < 2x + 3 \le 11\]

How many integers \(x\) satisfy the inequality?
questions.solution_title: Do the same to all three parts
questions.solution:
\[\begin{aligned} -10 &< 2x \le 8 \\ -5 &< x \le 4 \end{aligned}\]

The integers are \(-4, -3, \ldots, 4\): \(\boxed{9}\) of them. \(-5\) is not included (strict \(<\)); 4 is.

takeaway: Solve like an equation, flip the sign for a negative multiplier, and round whole-number answers in the direction the limit allows.
